verdict.rationale: Ramp documents OAuth 2.0 with granular resource:permission scopes, client-credentials grants, and explicit least-privilege guidance ("configure only the scopes your app needs"). It also offers an agent identity model with one key per agent, each tied to a human sponsor and given flexible permissions, plus browserless agent login for the CLI. A live probe confirms the MCP server is OAuth-gated with granular read/write scopes. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of actually issuing a per-agent scoped key end-to-end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: configure only the scopes your app needs.
One key per agent — tied to a human sponsor on your team. Flexible permissions — decide what each agent can read and do.
Standalone agents authenticate without a browser by exchanging OAuth client credentials for a production access token
Ramp uses OAuth 2.0 for secure API access, providing granular permission control through scopes and supporting multiple authorization flows for different use cases.
